concepts.definition: LLM-first, graph-first algebraic governance control language with native typed declarative syntax, explicit validator/HoG/ABG boundaries and strong typed contract-law anti-drift judgments.

grounding.quote:
Define GTL 3 as an LLM-first, graph-first, algebraic governance control
language with host-language-native typed declarative syntax and explicit
GTL-validator-HoG-ABG boundaries.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-001**: GTL shall be an LLM-first, graph-first,
algebraic governance control language with host-language-native typed
declarative syntax.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-002**: Each conformant build tenant shall publish GTL as
an embedded typed declaration surface in its host language plus an equivalent
serialized admission carrier. GTL shall not require a separate free-form
programming syntax or parser family beyond those published contracts.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-009**: GTL shall use strong typed axioms and
validator-visible contract law as its anti-drift mechanism for LLM-authored
programs. Graph, program, start, implementation, result-interface, catalog,
carrier, traversal, and bind declarations shall produce typed validity, typed
invalidity, or typed unresolved semantics without lowering into an executable
intermediate program.

concepts.label: GTL language

concepts.definition: Qualified index of GTL capabilities and requirement traces used for review/validation, not runtime lookup or traversal selection.

grounding.quote:
**language capability catalog**: A qualified index of GTL language
capabilities and their requirement traces. It is a review and validation aid.
It is not a runtime lookup registry and not traversal selection truth.

**catalog**: A qualified index surface. The word catalog shall not stand alone
as authority. A catalog reference shall state whether it is a language
capability catalog, publication inventory, library index, conformance catalog,
consequence catalog, runtime registry query, or another named catalog family.

concepts.label: Language capability catalog

concepts.definition: Static declaration/admission inventory demonstrating claimed Module, Program or bundle publication scope, usable for conformance but not live lookup or selection.

grounding.quote:
**publication inventory**: A static GTL declaration or admission inventory that
proves a module, program, or bundle publishes the surfaces it claims. A
publication inventory may support conformance checks. It is not a live lookup
registry and not traversal selection truth.

concepts.label: Publication inventory

concepts.definition: ABG-owned admitted lookup concept over registered eligible surfaces; querying registered entries does not select traversal.

grounding.quote:
**runtime registry**: An ABG-owned admitted lookup concept over registered
runtime-eligible surfaces. A runtime registry may expose query results, but any
candidate choice that affects traversal shall become ABG-emitted selection
truth before it has runtime authority.

concepts.label: Runtime registry

concepts.definition: Reusable publication set of callables, overlays, candidate families, starts, policies or companions. It may be system/upstream or Product/downstream owned and is not registry truth before ABG admission/projection.

grounding.quote:
**library**: A reusable publication set of declared graph functions, overlays,
candidate families, public starts, policies, or companion surfaces. A graph
function in a library is a reusable workflow function, not the whole product
program. A library may be upstream/system-owned or downstream/product-owned. A
library is not a runtime registry until ABG admits and projects its entries
into registry truth.

concepts.label: Library

concepts.definition: GTL/ABG-owned generic callables and companions needed identically by multiple ODD domains and admitted through common authority.

grounding.quote:
**system library**: A GTL/ABG-owned library of generic graph functions and
related surfaces needed identically across multiple ODD domains. System
library entries shall be admitted through GTL/ABG authority and shall not be
reimplemented by downstream products as parallel system truth.

concepts.label: System library

concepts.definition: Downstream-owned specialized GTL callables, overlays, policies or candidate families, lawful only through GTL declaration and ABG admission subordinate to runtime authority.

grounding.quote:
**product library**: A downstream-owned GTL library of specialized graph
functions, overlays, policies, or candidate families. Product library entries
are lawful only when declared through GTL, admitted by ABG, and kept subordinate
to ABG runtime authority.

concepts.label: Product library

concepts.definition: ABG truth surface derived from emitted events, admitted payloads or replay projection, never a rival mutable Product store/controller memory.

grounding.quote:
**ledger**: An ABG-owned truth surface derived from emitted events, admitted
payloads, or replay-derived projection. A ledger shall not mean a product-local
mutable store, controller memory, or second authority over fold, residual,
admission, continuation, re-entry, or selection truth.

concepts.label: ABG ledger

concepts.definition: Append-only recording path for admitted runtime facts whose traversal, closure, selection, continuation and re-entry truth cannot be replaced by local computation/memory.

grounding.quote:
**event stream**: The append-only runtime truth path used by ABG to record
admitted runtime facts. Runtime truth that affects traversal, closure,
selection, continuation, or re-entry shall not be replaced by query-local
calculation or product-local memory.

concepts.label: ABG event stream

concepts.definition: Replay-derived view that may join, render, classify or summarize admitted facts without inventing truth absent from its governing source.

grounding.quote:
**projection**: A replay-derived view over admitted truth. A projection may
join, render, classify, or summarize admitted facts. A projection shall not
invent runtime truth that was not admitted or emitted by its governing source
surface.

concepts.label: Projection

concepts.definition: Consumer query/interpretation over admitted truth or projections that may label domain meaning but cannot mutate runtime authority.

grounding.quote:
**read model**: A consumer-facing query or interpretation surface over admitted
truth or projections. A read model may label domain meaning. It shall not
admit evidence, emit events, fold assurance, select traversal, close, continue,
or re-enter.

concepts.label: Read model

concepts.definition: GTL/conformance declaration or index of Program composition over callables, vectors, node types, starts, roles, security, policy, proofs, plugin/result contracts and related metadata, not traversal control.

grounding.quote:
**overlay row**: A GTL or conformance declaration row that declares or indexes
a program composition over graph functions, graph vectors, node types, starts,
roles, security, policy, proof obligations, plugin/result contracts, and
related metadata. An overlay row is not a traversal controller.

concepts.label: Overlay row

concepts.definition: ABG runtime observation, pressure or foldback contract scoped to admitted state, distinct from GTL overlay rows.

grounding.quote:
**overlay frame**: An ABG runtime observation, pressure, or foldback contract
scoped to admitted runtime state. An overlay frame belongs to ABG runtime law
and is distinct from an overlay row.

concepts.label: Overlay frame

concepts.definition: GTL-declared graph-function alternatives preserving one explicit outer contract; membership itself selects no candidate.

grounding.quote:
**candidate family**: A GTL-declared family of graph-function candidates that
share an explicit outer contract. Candidate-family membership does not select
a candidate for traversal.

concepts.label: Candidate family

concepts.definition: ABG-emitted/admitted runtime truth recording a traversal-affecting candidate choice after any queries, filters or ranking.

grounding.quote:
**selection event**: ABG-emitted truth recording a traversal-affecting
candidate choice. Selection may be preceded by queries, eligibility filters,
or ranking, but the runtime effect belongs to the emitted selection event.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-021**: A selection event shall be
ABG-admitted truth whenever candidate choice affects traversal. `F_D`, `F_P`,
or `F_H` ranking may propose selection only through the declared GTL boundary;
ABG validates and admits the resulting identity and HoG applies it. Neither ABG
nor the proposing implementation owns a hidden selection policy.

concepts.label: Selection event

concepts.definition: Query of admitted registry truth returning candidates or rejection diagnostics for a named situation; it may inform, but does not constitute, traversal selection.

grounding.quote:
**runtime lookup**: A query over admitted registry truth that returns lawful or
rejected candidates for a named situation. Runtime lookup may inform selection.
It does not become selection authority until ABG emits selection truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-019**: Runtime lookup shall return
candidates or rejection diagnostics over admitted registry truth. Runtime
lookup shall not become traversal authority. A declared GTL selector or
attributed external decision proposes the selected identity, ABG admits that
identity as runtime truth, and HoG follows the admitted program relation.

concepts.label: Runtime lookup

concepts.definition: Deterministic ABG-owned check of candidate identity, interface, source/target contracts, context, authority, overlay, namespace, version, provenance, readiness, proof and policy.

grounding.quote:
**eligibility filter**: A deterministic ABG-owned filter over candidate
identity, interface, source and target contracts, context, authority, overlay,
namespace, version, provenance, readiness, proof, and policy constraints.

concepts.label: Eligibility filter

concepts.definition: Product-visible entry handle bound to a published GraphFunction, not a bare vector or owner of execution truth.

grounding.quote:
**public start**: A product-visible entry handle bound to a published graph
function. A public start is not a bare graph vector and does not own runtime
execution truth.

concepts.label: Public start

concepts.definition: Named node contract with typed identity, published noncallably through the GTL library path as registry kind node_type for references, type composition, satisfaction and type-sensitive GraphFunction composition.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-026**: GTL shall provide one reusable
node-type capability for declaring named node contracts, binding nodes to
type refs, composing node types, checking type satisfaction, and composing
graph functions by endpoint type satisfaction.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-027**: A node type shall be published
through the GTL library path as a non-callable node-type declaration with its
own typed identity and the `node_type` registry kind. It shall not mint or use
a `GraphFunction` identity, and no parallel type publication path is lawful.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-028**: A `node_type` library entry may
be admitted, projected, imported, queried, and used by validator/conformance
surfaces. It shall not become runtime traversal work, public-start authority,
graph-call authority, or `graph_function_selected` truth.

concepts.label: Reusable node type

concepts.definition: Requirement-family role of stating governing GTL 3 language laws; the supplied excerpt contains its purpose only.

grounding.quote: State the governing language laws of GTL 3.

concepts.label: GTL governing language laws

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-001**: GTL shall publish one language
capability model that lets reviewers identify every language-level capability
without reading implementation source or downstream product conventions.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-002**: The language capability model
shall distinguish GTL declaration capability from ABG runtime realization.
GTL may declare, constrain, compose, publish, and validate program law; ABG
owns admission, event truth, runtime ledgers, projection, fold, continuation,
re-entry, and traversal-affecting selection.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-003**: Each GTL capability shall state
purpose, owner, authority boundary, source truth, admitted inputs, emitted
truth if any, projection outputs, query outputs, rejection taxonomy, readiness
gates, proof obligations, invariants, forbidden authority, and downstream
interpretation boundary.

constraints.statement: Publish one complete language-level capability model accessible without implementation source or downstream convention. Every capability states purpose, owner, authority boundary, source truth, admitted inputs, emitted truth if any, projection/query outputs, rejection taxonomy, readiness gates, proof obligations, invariants, forbidden authority and downstream interpretation boundary.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-002**: The language capability model
shall distinguish GTL declaration capability from ABG runtime realization.
GTL may declare, constrain, compose, publish, and validate program law; ABG
owns admission, event truth, runtime ledgers, projection, fold, continuation,
re-entry, and traversal-affecting selection.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-003**: Each GTL capability shall state
purpose, owner, authority boundary, source truth, admitted inputs, emitted
truth if any, projection outputs, query outputs, rejection taxonomy, readiness
gates, proof obligations, invariants, forbidden authority, and downstream
interpretation boundary.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-004**: HOW design shall treat carrier
names, module boundaries, API spellings, event names, data structures, tests,
and proof artifacts as implementation bindings to WHAT. HOW design shall not
change ownership, authority, invariants, or semantic boundaries declared by
WHAT.

constraints.statement: GTL declares, constrains, composes, publishes and validates law; ABG owns admission/events/ledgers/projection/fold/continuation/re-entry/traversal selection. HOW carrier names, modules, APIs, events, structures, tests and proof artifacts bind WHAT without changing owners, authority, invariants or meaning.

grounding.quote:
**catalog**: A qualified index surface. The word catalog shall not stand alone
as authority. A catalog reference shall state whether it is a language
capability catalog, publication inventory, library index, conformance catalog,
consequence catalog, runtime registry query, or another named catalog family.

**publication inventory**: A static GTL declaration or admission inventory that
proves a module, program, or bundle publishes the surfaces it claims. A
publication inventory may support conformance checks. It is not a live lookup
registry and not traversal selection truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-005**: A language capability catalog
shall be a qualified index of GTL capabilities and requirement traces. It
shall not be treated as a runtime registry, runtime lookup result, or
selection event.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-006**: A publication inventory shall
prove declared publication scope only. It shall not be treated as a runtime
registry, runtime lookup result, or selection event.

constraints.statement: Catalog never supplies authority by its bare name; qualify references as capability catalog, publication inventory, library index, conformance catalog, consequence catalog, runtime registry query or another named family. Capability catalog and static publication inventory do not constitute a runtime registry, lookup result or selection event; inventory proves publication scope only.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-007**: A runtime registry shall be an
ABG-owned admitted lookup concept. Runtime registry truth shall be derived from
declared and admitted entries, not from product-local lists, prompt prose,
manual scans, or controller memory.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-023**: A runtime registry design shall
be non-conformant if it is built from static publication inventory alone,
product-local configuration, prompt-only context, manual discovery, or
query-local candidate selection without admitted registry truth.

constraints.statement: Registry truth derives from declared/admitted entries, not Product lists, prose, manual scanning or controller memory. A design based solely on static inventory, local configuration, prompt-only context, manual discovery or query-local selection without admitted registry truth is nonconforming.

exceptions: Explicit declared refinement, override or specialization law plus accepted ABG eligibility proof permits a Product entry to override a system entry.

grounding.quote:
**library**: A reusable publication set of declared graph functions, overlays,
candidate families, public starts, policies, or companion surfaces. A graph
function in a library is a reusable workflow function, not the whole product
program. A library may be upstream/system-owned or downstream/product-owned. A
library is not a runtime registry until ABG admits and projects its entries
into registry truth.

**system library**: A GTL/ABG-owned library of generic graph functions and
related surfaces needed identically across multiple ODD domains. System
library entries shall be admitted through GTL/ABG authority and shall not be
reimplemented by downstream products as parallel system truth.

**product library**: A downstream-owned GTL library of specialized graph
functions, overlays, policies, or candidate families. Product library entries
are lawful only when declared through GTL, admitted by ABG, and kept subordinate
to ABG runtime authority.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-008**: A system library shall contain
generic GTL/ABG-owned graph functions or companion surfaces that multiple ODD
domains need identically. Downstream products shall not republish a system
library function as parallel authority.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-009**: A product library shall be
lawful when it declares product-specialized graph functions or companion
surfaces through GTL and ABG admits those entries. Product libraries shall not
bypass declaration, admission, provenance, proof, readiness, or ownership
checks.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-010**: A product library shall not
shadow, replace, or override a system library entry unless explicit
refinement, override, or specialization law is declared and ABG eligibility
proof accepts it.

constraints.statement: A library callable remains a reusable function, not a whole Program. System entries are common-authority admissions and may not be republished as downstream parallel truth. Product entries must pass declaration, admission, provenance, proof, readiness and ownership checks; they may shadow/replace/override system entries only under explicit refinement/override/specialization law accepted by ABG eligibility proof.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-011**: A ledger shall be an ABG-owned
event or projection truth surface. A product-local mutable store shall not be
called a ledger when it would compete with ABG admission, event, fold,
residual, continuation, re-entry, registry, or selection truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-012**: An event stream shall remain
the append-only truth path for runtime facts. Query-local calculation,
side-array return values, product-local files, or controller memory shall not
replace the event stream for traversal-affecting truth.

constraints.statement: Product-local mutable stores must not masquerade as ledgers competing with ABG admission/events/fold/residual/continuation/re-entry/registry/selection. The append-only event path cannot be replaced for traversal-affecting truth by query-local calculations, side-array returns, local files or controller memory.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-013**: A projection shall be
replay-derived from admitted source truth. A projection shall not create fold,
residual, registry, selection, continuation, or re-entry truth that its source
truth did not admit or emit.

constraints.statement: Projection stays replay-derived from admitted source and creates no fold, residual, registry, selection, continuation or re-entry truth not admitted/emitted by that source.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-014**: A read model shall be
read-only. It may interpret or label admitted truth for a consumer, but it
shall not emit events, admit evidence, fold assurance, select traversal, close,
continue, or re-enter.

constraints.statement: Consumer interpretation and labels are allowed, but no event emission, evidence admission, assurance fold, traversal selection, close, continue or re-entry.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-015**: An overlay row shall be program
composition, catalog, publication, public-start, graph-function, graph-vector,
node-type, role, security, policy, proof-obligation, plugin/result-contract, or
related metadata. An overlay row shall not own runtime observation, pressure,
foldback, continuation, or selection authority.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-016**: An overlay frame shall be ABG
runtime contract truth over observed state, pressure, or foldback. An overlay
frame shall not be treated as a GTL publication inventory row or downstream
product controller.

constraints.statement: Rows declare/index Program metadata and never own observation, pressure, foldback, continuation or selection. Frames are ABG contracts over observed state/pressure/foldback, never inventory rows or Product controllers.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-015A**: GTL shall distinguish the
library/program/workspace abstraction boundary. Graph functions are reusable
library functions or callable work contracts. Graph overlays or GTL program
compositions are the program surfaces that bind those functions. Workspaces are
mutable instance surfaces that supply bootstrap config, files, data, observed
state, generated artifacts, and run archives. HoG traversal is the execution
bind over admitted program and workspace truth; ABG admits its runtime facts.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-015B**: Overlays shall bind compositions
over graphs; graphs shall compose nested graph calls and declared computations
under the same HoG execution law. Reference-frame evaluation contracts shall

constraints.statement: GraphFunctions are reusable callable/library contracts; overlays/Program compositions bind them as the Program. Workspaces are mutable bootstrap/config/files/data/observation/artifact/archive instance surfaces. HoG executes against admitted Program/workspace binding; ABG admits facts. Overlays bind graphs; graphs compose nested calls and declared computation under one HoG law.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-015B**: Overlays shall bind compositions
over graphs; graphs shall compose nested graph calls and declared computations
under the same HoG execution law. Reference-frame evaluation contracts shall
be reusable through existing composition, Context, contract and policy
declarations under `REQ-L-GTL3-CONTEXT-009..012`. First-class frame use shall not
introduce a separate topology object, callable kind, registry or interpreter.
The frame contract, overlay composition and ABG runtime Frame shall retain
their distinct meanings.

constraints.statement: Reusable evaluation-frame contracts use existing composition, Context, contract and policy declarations under CONTEXT-009..012. First-class frame use adds no topology kind, callable kind, registry or interpreter. Keep frame-contract meaning, overlay composition and ABG runtime Frame distinct.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-017**: A candidate family shall
preserve one explicit outer contract across its candidates. Candidate-family
membership shall not select a candidate for traversal.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-018**: A public start shall bind to a
published graph function. A public start shall not expose a bare graph vector
as product-visible runtime authority.

constraints.statement: Every candidate shares one explicit outer contract and membership selects none. Public starts bind published callables and cannot expose bare vectors as Product-visible runtime authority.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-019**: Runtime lookup shall return
candidates or rejection diagnostics over admitted registry truth. Runtime
lookup shall not become traversal authority. A declared GTL selector or
attributed external decision proposes the selected identity, ABG admits that
identity as runtime truth, and HoG follows the admitted program relation.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-020**: An eligibility filter shall
account for candidate identity, interface, source contracts, target contracts,
context, authority, overlay scope, namespace, version, provenance, readiness,
proof state, and policy refs before a candidate can be selected.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-021**: A selection event shall be
ABG-admitted truth whenever candidate choice affects traversal. `F_D`, `F_P`,
or `F_H` ranking may propose selection only through the declared GTL boundary;
ABG validates and admits the resulting identity and HoG applies it. Neither ABG
nor the proposing implementation owns a hidden selection policy.

constraints.statement: A declared GTL selector or attributed external decision proposes identity; ABG validates/admit-emits its runtime selection truth and HoG follows the admitted Program relation. F_D/F_P/F_H ranking can propose only through declared GTL boundaries. Neither ABG nor the proposing implementation may own hidden selection policy; lookup is not traversal authority.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-020**: An eligibility filter shall
account for candidate identity, interface, source contracts, target contracts,
context, authority, overlay scope, namespace, version, provenance, readiness,
proof state, and policy refs before a candidate can be selected.

constraints.statement: Before selection account for identity, interface, source/target contracts, context, authority, overlay scope, namespace, version, provenance, readiness, proof state and policy references.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-022**: Implementation-specific HOW
accounts, GTL-validator capability maps, and spec-vs-implementation gap
tables shall not be written into this requirement family. They are design or
commentary read models over the live requirement surface.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-025**: Gap analysis shall classify
differences between WHAT and implementation as terminology gaps,
requirement gaps, design gaps, implementation gaps, proof gaps,
documentation gaps, or deferred runtime-registry gaps. Gap analysis shall not
replace live requirement truth.

constraints.statement: Keep HOW accounts, validator capability maps and spec/implementation gap tables in design/commentary read models, outside this requirement family. Gap analysis classifies terminology, requirement, design, implementation, proof, documentation or deferred runtime-registry gaps and never replaces live WHAT.

exceptions: Demonstrated genericity across ODD domains permits system-level treatment.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-024**: Downstream domain semantics such
as software test, build, release, language toolchain, service protocol, or
product lifecycle policy shall not be promoted into GTL/ABG system-library
law. Such semantics belong in downstream product libraries, plugins, or read
models unless proven generic across ODD domains.

constraints.statement: Software test/build/release, toolchain, service protocol and Product lifecycle policies remain downstream library/plugin/read-model meanings rather than system-library law unless proven generic across ODD domains.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-026**: GTL shall provide one reusable
node-type capability for declaring named node contracts, binding nodes to
type refs, composing node types, checking type satisfaction, and composing
graph functions by endpoint type satisfaction.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-027**: A node type shall be published
through the GTL library path as a non-callable node-type declaration with its
own typed identity and the `node_type` registry kind. It shall not mint or use
a `GraphFunction` identity, and no parallel type publication path is lawful.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-028**: A `node_type` library entry may
be admitted, projected, imported, queried, and used by validator/conformance
surfaces. It shall not become runtime traversal work, public-start authority,
graph-call authority, or `graph_function_selected` truth.

constraints.statement: Use one reusable capability and the GTL library publication path with typed identity and node_type kind. No GraphFunction identity or parallel type publication path. Entries may be admitted, projected, imported, queried or used for validation/conformance, but never traversal work, public-start/graph-call authority or graph_function_selected truth.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-029**: Type conformance shall be pure,
deterministic, replayable, and fail-closed. Unknown type refs, digest drift,
weakened schema, markov, context, asset-surface, authority, proof, or output
obligations shall reject rather than infer compatibility.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-030**: Composed node types shall
preserve or strengthen every constituent node-type obligation. Composition
shall not weaken required schema, markov, asset-surface, authority, proof,
output, context, or provenance obligations.

constraints.statement: Conformance is pure, deterministic, replayable and fail-closed. Reject unknown type references, digest drift or weakened schema, Markov, context, AssetSurface, authority, proof or output obligations rather than infer compatibility. Composed types preserve or strengthen every constituent obligation, including provenance.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-002**: Each conformant build tenant shall publish GTL as
an embedded typed declaration surface in its host language plus an equivalent
serialized admission carrier. GTL shall not require a separate free-form
programming syntax or parser family beyond those published contracts.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-003**: GTL shall be declarative. It shall declare lawful structure, contracts, hook attachment points, and semantic work surfaces rather than constructive tactics or hidden strategy.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-006**: GTL shall not define a specialized in-language policy semantic language. It shall expose hook attachment points and opaque configuration only.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-007**: GTL shall remain graph-function-first, composition-first, recursion-capable, higher-order, engine-agnostic, and governance-visible without prescribing constructive tactics.

constraints.statement: Each conformant tenant publishes embedded native typed declarations and equivalent serialized admission; no separate free-form syntax/parser family is required. GTL declares structure/contracts/hooks/work surfaces, never constructive tactics or hidden strategy. It stays graph-function-first, composition-first, recursive, higher-order, engine-agnostic and governance-visible, with opaque hook config rather than a policy semantic DSL.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-004**: GTL constructs shall be directly traversable by
conformant executor frameworks. HoG is the ABIogenesis executor. ABG is the
runtime-truth substrate around execution, not a second language or executor.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-005**: GTL owns language law, programs, graph structure,
contracts, algebra, and declared seams. The GTL validator owns non-lowering
whole-program judgment. HoG owns direct traversal. ABG owns runtime admission,
events, replay, lineage, provenance, correction, continuation, and closure.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-009**: GTL shall use strong typed axioms and
validator-visible contract law as its anti-drift mechanism for LLM-authored
programs. Graph, program, start, implementation, result-interface, catalog,
carrier, traversal, and bind declarations shall produce typed validity, typed
invalidity, or typed unresolved semantics without lowering into an executable
intermediate program.

constraints.statement: GTL owns law/programs/graphs/contracts/algebra/seams; validator owns non-lowering whole-program judgment; HoG is direct executor; ABG is runtime-truth substrate owning admission/events/replay/lineage/provenance/correction/continuation/closure, neither a second language nor executor. grounding.quote:
**runtime lookup**: A query over admitted registry truth that returns lawful or
rejected candidates for a named situation. Runtime lookup may inform selection.
It does not become selection authority until ABG emits selection truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-019**: Runtime lookup shall return
candidates or rejection diagnostics over admitted registry truth. Runtime
lookup shall not become traversal authority. A declared GTL selector or
attributed external decision proposes the selected identity, ABG admits that
identity as runtime truth, and HoG follows the admitted program relation.

relations.meaning: Lookup returns candidates/rejections from admitted registry truth while withholding traversal authority.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-LANGUAGE-CAPABILITY-MODEL-020**: An eligibility filter shall
account for candidate identity, interface, source contracts, target contracts,
context, authority, overlay scope, namespace, version, provenance, readiness,
proof state, and policy refs before a candidate can be selected.

ABG validates and admits the resulting identity and HoG applies it. Neither ABG
nor the proposing implementation owns a hidden selection policy.

library is not a runtime registry until ABG admits and projects its entries
into registry truth.
